this little pig went to market

terms.comment: Our title for the rhyme, one little pig to each toe, with porcellus, the classical word for a piglet (Varro, Suetonius). No ancient toe-counting rhyme is known; the rhyme below is ours, on the English one.

phrases.latin: Hic porcellus in forum iit; hic porcellus domī mānsit; hic porcellus assum ēdit; hic porcellus nihil accēpit; hic porcellus vāgiēns domum cucurrit.
phrases.english: This little piggy went to market; this little piggy stayed at home; this little piggy had roast meat; this little piggy had none; and this little piggy ran home squealing.

sources: Lewis & Short: porcellus · Lewis & Short: assus · Lewis & Short: vagio
No ancient toe-counting rhyme is known; the title and the rhyme are ours. Assum is a roast (Cic. Fam. 9.20, assum vitulīnum), and vāgīre is used of swine (Mart. 3.58.37), both in Lewis & Short.
The example sentence marked “composed” is ours.
